title: Fiber Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Send a greeting
entries.summary: A Fiber handler returns an error value. SendString writes the response text. Open GET /hello.

example.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Get("/hello", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.SendString("Hello, Asha!") })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}

notes: Return the error from response-writing methods.

entries.name: Send named data
entries.summary: JSON writes an object as JSON. Open GET /book.

example.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Get("/book", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.JSON(fiber.Map{"title": "Moon Trip"}) })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}

notes: Use the Fiber v2 context pointer shown in this course.

entries.name: Read a route value
entries.summary: Params reads a named path part. Open GET /hello/Ravi.

example.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Get("/hello/:name", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.SendString("Hi, " + c.Params("name") + "!") })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}

entries.name: Read a query string
entries.summary: Query reads a query value and can take a default. Open GET /page.

example.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Get("/page", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.JSON(fiber.Map{"page": c.Query("n", "1")}) })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}

notes: A query value remains text until you parse it.

entries.name: Parse an integer input
entries.summary: ParamsInt parses a route value as an integer. Open GET /double/4.

example.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Get("/double/:n", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { n, err := c.ParamsInt("n"); if err != nil { return c.Status(400).SendString("Use a whole number") }; return c.JSON(fiber.Map{"answer": n * 2}) })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}

notes: Check the error before using the parsed number.

entries.name: Read a body into a struct
entries.summary: BodyParser fills a struct from the request body. Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}.
notes: Parsing does not replace checks for a useful field value.

entries.name: Group routes
entries.summary: Group adds a shared path prefix. Open GET /api/books.

example.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
api := app.Group("/api")
api.Get("/books", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.JSON([]string{"Moon Trip"}) })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}

notes: Request the group prefix as well as the inner path.

entries.name: Share request data
entries.summary: Locals stores a value for the current request. A middleware can set it before a route reads it.

example.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Use(func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { c.Locals("school", "Oak School"); return c.Next() })
app.Get("/school", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.SendString(c.Locals("school").(string)) })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}

notes: Check a value type if it may come from a different source.

entries.name: Set a reply header
entries.summary: Set adds a response header. Open GET /note and inspect Cache-Control.

example.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Get("/note", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { c.Set("Cache-Control", "no-store"); return c.SendString("Practice note") })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}

notes: Set headers before sending the body.

entries.name: Point to another route
entries.summary: Redirect sends a location and status. A browser following GET /start reaches /hello.

example.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Get("/start", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.Redirect("/hello", 302) })
app.Get("/hello", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.SendString("Welcome") })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}

notes: A redirect requires another client request.

entries.name: Reply with a missing-item status
entries.summary: Status selects a code before a body is sent. Open GET /missing.

example.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Get("/missing", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.Status(404).JSON(fiber.Map{"error": "Book not found"}) })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}

notes: A helpful error body should keep the correct error status.

entries.name: Handle an unknown URL
entries.summary: A final Use handler can reply when no earlier route handled the request. Open GET /unknown.

example.code:
package main
import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
func main() {
app := fiber.New()
app.Get("/", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.SendString("Home") })
app.Use(func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.Status(404).SendString("Page not found") })
app.Listen("127.0.0.1:3000")
}

notes: Put a catch-all handler after the real routes.
